chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Chris Columbo on a motorcycle seat and 18-year-old arranger Oliver Nelson
summary: He recalls drummer Chris Columbo's showmanship, the teenager who wrote the whole book, and trumpeter Money Johnson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: During that period, I had the pleasure of working with some musicians that I made friends with for life. One of them was a fellow everybody calls Christopher Columbus -- Chris Columbo. He is a drummer, and I guess Chris should be in his middle seventies or close to eighty years old -- I understand he's still playing in Atlantic City. He had a very unique way of playing. The seat that he used when he played drums was a motorcycle seat, and he jumped up and down, which was a very attractive thing to people when they saw him doing it, and I
guess it made it kind of a show thing for the band.

But one of the most, I would say, significant people in the band, for more than one reason, was a young man who was 18 years old at that particular time. His name was Oliver Nelson. I was amazed at this guy, because he had written the whole book for the band, and it was rather an extensive book. Besides all of Louis' things, he'd written a lot of other original things. And he played saxophone very well.
Money Johnson, another trumpet player, was in the band. And of course, the guy who was responsible for me being there, Pee Wee Moore, was there.
